𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐞𝐞𝐫 𝐇𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫, 𝟏𝟗𝟕𝟖.⁣
⁣
No, The Deer Hunter (1978) is not the best Vietnam War film ever made. It’s hardly about Vietnam at all. This isn’t Apocalypse Now (1979) or Platoon (1986). Michael Cimino’s film isn’t interested in recreating the war. He is interested in the people. The ordinary small-town Americans before, during, and after the Vietnam War. That’s why it hits harder than any “war movie.” You recognize these people. They could be your uncles, your friends, your drinking buddies at the bar after a long shift at the steel mill.⁣
⁣
A lot of people complain about the first hour: “too long,” “too slow,” “nothing happens.” Bullsh*t. That’s the point. Those endless wedding scenes, those hunting trips, those stupid macho jokes… they’re the setup. They show you the innocence and the bonds between these guys. And because Cimino makes you live in their small Pennsylvania town, the contrast with what comes later is devastating. Without that first hour, the Russian Roulette scenes don’t carry half the weight.⁣
⁣
Ah yes… the Russian Roulette. Even today, it’s one of the most intense sequence I’ve ever seen on film. Robert De Niro and Christopher Walken forced to play death as a game. And later, when Walken’s Nick has disappeared into the underworld of Saigon, playing the same game for money, already lost in his own broken mind… It’s unbearable. “Mike who?” he asks De Niro, unable to recognize his best friend. Walken has never been better. He won the Oscar, and deservedly so. ⁣
⁣
What The Deer Hunter (1978) is really about is aftermath. About how war doesn’t end when you come home. About how it fractures people, friendships and entire communities. When I first saw it, I thought: this is one of the greatest movies ever made… Watching it hurts. It still hurts. And yet I want you to see it. Because The Deer Hunter (1979) remains one of the most haunting works of American cinema. source_details.title: The Deer Hunter
source_details.synopsis: The Deer Hunter is a 1978 American epic war drama film co-written and directed by Michael Cimino about a trio of Russian-American steelworkers (inspired by Cimino's real-life Belarusian-American friend) whose lives are upended by fighting in the Vietnam War. The soldiers are played by Robert De Niro, Christopher Walken and John Savage, with John Cazale (in his final role), Meryl Streep, and George Dzundza in supporting roles. The story takes place in Clairton, Pennsylvania (a working-class town on the Monongahela River south of Pittsburgh) and in Vietnam.
